name: Steppe Warhorse Breeds
description: Domesticate swift, enduring steppe ponies bred for cavalry maneuvering and endurance.
creativePrompt: How did the tribes first tame the wild herds? What bond exists between rider and foal?
exampleNarrative: Stout, shaggy steppe ponies with barrel chests and tireless hooves transformed the hunters into a lightning-fast host.

name: Heavy Draft Oxen & Plows
description: Yoke massive horned oxen to heavy iron-tipped plows, breaking deep river valley soils.
creativePrompt: How did the introduction of ox teams multiply the annual grain harvest?
exampleNarrative: Teams of sturdy black oxen cut deep furrows through the rich alluvial clay, turning wild meadows into vast grainfields.

name: Golden Spelt & Ancient Wheat
description: Cultivate nutritious heirloom cereal grains that yield bountiful flour and golden bread.
creativePrompt: Which harvest deity was thanked for the first wild grain seeds? How are granaries defended?
exampleNarrative: Vast golden wheatfields rippled in the autumn winds, filling underground stone silos with grain for hard winters.

name: Terraced Mountain Paddy Rice
description: Engineer flooded mountain terraces capturing glacial runoff for high-yield aquatic rice.
creativePrompt: How are the water sluices coordinated between uphill and downhill farmers?
exampleNarrative: Glistening emerald terraces climbed the steep mountain slopes, mirroring the clouds in their quiet flooded pools.

name: Bog & Magnetite Iron Lodes
description: Harvest rich peat-bog iron and mountain magnetite ore for strong plowshares and weapons.
creativePrompt: How did the discovery of iron tools supplant stone and copper tools?
exampleNarrative: Smelters coaxed spongy blooms of raw iron from charcoal furnaces, outfitting every warrior with heavy spearheads.

name: Deep Vein Silver & Electrum
description: Strike veins of pure native silver and electrum, founding jewelry crafts and trade coinage.
creativePrompt: Which kings put their stamp on the first silver bullion ingots? Who guards the royal mines?
exampleNarrative: Miners uncovered veins of shimmering native silver, providing the wealth that would fund kingdoms and treaties.

name: Ancient Tall Shipmast Pines
description: Harvest straight, resin-rich primeval pines prized for longships, roof beams, and palisades.
creativePrompt: What rituals must woodsmen perform to appease the dryads before felling a great patriarch tree?
exampleNarrative: Giant hundred-foot pines were floated downriver to the shipyards, their dense grain forming hulls that could brave ocean storms.

name: Sun-Mithril & Sky-Beasts
description: Discover veins of weightless solar mithril and tame winged sky-drakes upon the cloud peaks.
creativePrompt: How light is solar mithril? How does a champion earn the loyalty of a hatched sky-beast?
exampleNarrative: Forged from feathers of fallen stars, the glowing mithril mail was light as linen yet turned aside the sharpest lance.
